title: The local market and product costs
summary: Prices in Supermarket Simulator come from somewhere: the game keeps a local market with a product database, a product cost and a price display, so what you pay and what you charge are tracked, not invented.
body: The game keeps its own product database for the market, which is why costs can change without you editing anything on the shelf.
Cost and display price are separate things in that market data, so the number you paid and the number a customer sees are two different numbers.
There is a shopping cart and a store controller in the same system, which is why the market behaves like a place you interact with rather than a static price list.
The cart carries a record of its own. The build keeps cart data alongside the cart object, which is why what a cart holds can be read by the game and not only by the player pushing it.
What this entry does not tell you: how fast prices move, by how much, or which goods move first. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game keeps a local market with its own product database.
A product cost and a displayed price are tracked separately.
The market system includes a shopping cart and a store controller.
The build keeps cart data of its own.
Cleanliness is tracked against the shop's standing.
